main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} For every integer $n\ge1$ and every recursively enumerable set $S\subseteq\NN^n$, there are an integer $m\ge1$ and a polynomial $P\in\ZZ[A_1,\ldots,A_n,W_1,\ldots,W_m]$ such that, for every $a\in\NN^n$, \[ \#\{w\in\NN^m:P(a,w)=0\}= \begin{cases}1,&a\in S,\\0,&a\notin S.\end{cases} \] \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: Every r.e. set of natural-number tuples has a polynomial Diophantine representation over N in which each member has exactly one complete auxiliary witness tuple and each nonmember has none (Matiyasevich's single-fold conjecture, hence also the finite-fold conjecture).

corollary.paraphrase: There are fixed m, D such that solvability over N of polynomials in m variables of degree <= D is undecidable even under the promise of at most one solution.

proof_architecture.claim: Single-fold calculus: slacks, sign codes, conjunction/composition/disjoint cases with zeroed inactive variables, sum of squares.
Arithmetic on E: y^2=x^3-25x has E(Q)=ZP+E[2] (appendix descent); unique 6-coordinate rational codes and flagged point codes; single-fold addition and fixed scalar multiples.
Heights: W(Q)=H(x([m_*]Q)) depends only on |index| j and log W_j = a_E j^2 + O(c_E) with a_E tunable through m_*; representatives give one point per j.

Growth function: bracket selects k with W_k <= u+W_1 < W_{k+1}; square window pins the representative of index k^2; g(u)=W_{k^2} has a single-fold graph and growth exp(Theta((log u)^2)), i.e. between every polynomial and u^u.
Exponentiation: paired Pell equations with parameters bu and u, cutoff g(u), residues n+1 and integer quotient; u is a fixed polynomial in (c,b,n), so c=b^n and the whole witness are unique.
Binary containment via (B+1)^y digit extraction and Lucas mod 2.

Machine compiler: r.e. -> counter machine; encode the run in base B=2^w with masks; clock + dyadic window fix B; exactly one complete tuple per halting run; sum of squares gives Thm main; specialization gives the promise corollary.

lean_route_differences: Point addition: Lean AddEq has 5 cases and a slope-free relation Line d n (d^2(x3+x1+x2)=n^2, d(y3+y1)=n(x1-x3)) instead of 7 ordered cases with a local slope code (EllipticCoordinates.lean:96-145).
Disjoint cases: Lean uses Semi (both R and not R single-fold) and Representation.or with a selector and zeroed inactive blocks, rather than the paper's guard partition lemma.

Rank: full 2-descent with the Kummer map (alpha_0, alpha_5) into (Q*/Q*^2)^2 and an explicit generator G=(25/4,75/8) = (-4,6)+(0,0), instead of 2-isogeny descent; nontorsion of G by 2-adic valuation decreasing by 2 under doubling instead of Nagell-Lutz on (-4,6).
Torsion: E(Q)_tors = E[2] via strict height growth under doubling plus a kernel-checked enumeration of points of height < 185, instead of Nagell-Lutz.
Mordell-Weil and Neron-Tate: proved inside the family (generic height-descent theorem; Tate limit built on Mathlib's Weil height and addSubMap bound) instead of cited.
Universality: Mathlib ToPartrec.Code + PartrecToTM2 (TM2 with stacks) encoded by base-5 stack counters through a 'macro' counter machine, instead of the paper's one-tape TM two-stack simulation.
Pell: written as X^2 + F^2 = 1 + a^2 F^2 over N; Mathlib Pell.xn/yn.

eureka_candidates_ranked.name: Elliptic-height square window producing a single-fold growth function
for: Supplies exactly the object the 1974 problem lacked: a Diophantine relation of super-polynomial, sub-u^u growth whose graph is single-fold. Pell/Fibonacci relations fail because their solution sets are periodic in the index.

Key idea is tiny and non-obvious: because log W_j is quadratic in the hidden index with bounded error, a fixed product of heights at Q, 2Q, R, R+-P, P tests the quadratic relation r = k^2 exactly ((2k)^2 - 2k^2 - ((r+1)^2 - r^2) + 1 = 2(k^2 - r)). With linear log-growth (Pell) no bounded multiplicative test can square an index.
Neither elliptic curves nor heights occur in the goal or in the cited reduction; quick literature search found no Julia-Robinson relation built from canonical heights.
Load-bearing: growth dominates 49% of the Lean DAG and everything from Pow onward depends on it.
against: Rank-one curves and height or denominator growth are standard in Diophantine definability (Poonen 2002, cited; Denef; Shlapentokh; Eisentraeger-Everest), so the pivot from L may be one or two steps.

The target (single-fold exponential-growth relation suffices) was explicitly identified in the literature (Robinson 1952 reduction; cco2024 'replace exponentiation by any exponential-growth relation'). So the step answers a known sub-question rather than inventing the plan.
Neron-Tate quadraticity and the bounded error are textbook; the novelty is in how they are combined, which a judge may grade N2.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found on a line-by-line reading of all eight source files, and the Lean library (no sorry/axiom, Mathlib only) proves the comparator statement verbatim. Lean was not compiled here. The claim resolves a 1974 open problem, so independent build of the Lean and expert review remain necessary before treating it as settled.
checked: Rational codes: d=1 forces t=s=q=0; zero only with d=1; the inverse t is unique in [0,d-1] (Lean RationalCode.unique).
Height normalization: deg x = 2 so log H(x) - 2 hat h = O(1) matches Silverman VIII 9.3 with hat h = (1/2) lim 4^{-N} h_x.
W depends only on |n| because m_* is even and T = E[2]; log W_j = a_E j^2 + eps_j with a_E = 2 m_*^2 hat h(P).
Monotonicity: log W_{j+1} - log W_j >= a_E(2j+1) - 2c_E > 0 given a_E > 2c_E; W_1 > 1.
Representatives: x-coordinates in a coset jP+T are distinct (else 2jP torsion); exactly one of the two maximal points has y > 0.
Bracket: neighbour maximum is W_{k+1} for both signs of the index; unique k for every u including u = 0.
Window algebra: 4k^2 + r^2 + 1 - 2k^2 - (r+1)^2 = 2(k^2 - r); six error terms give |e| <= 6c_E < log kappa < 2a_E - 6c_E.
Growth: k^2 > log u/(8a_E) eventually, so log g >= a_E k^4 - c_E > (log u)^2/(128 a_E); upper bound O((log u)^2) < u log u.
Pell: index cutoff u^u < (2u-1)^{u-1} (f(4)=343/256); indices i,j in [1,u-1] pinned to n+1 by residues mod u-1 and bu-1 since n+1 < u-1.
Quotient: (1+z)^n - 1 <= nz/(1-nz); with u >= (c+1)(n+1)+4, 2u-1-n-cn >= cn+2c+n+9 > 0, so floor(F/H) = b^n.
Existence in Prop power: log F <= n log(2bu) <= 3(log u)^2/(l log 2) < delta (log u)^2 < log g(u), using u >= (c+1)^l > b^{nl}.
Binary containment: coefficients of (B+1)^y are < 2^y < B, so the extracted digit is binom(y,x); parity by Frobenius in F_2[Z].

Machine: digit sums < B (s < B, |A| <= 2s < B); summing state equations gives B I_h = 1 + (B-1)M = H, so the halt occurs exactly at time k-1; counter coefficients have |c_t| <= B/2; clock gives rho_0 = C+k-1 and B in (2(C+T),4(C+T)], unique power of two, B >= 8 so 4 | B.
Ledger counts: s+3tau+r+1 containment calls and r+5 comparison slacks match the system.
Appendix: (-4,6) lies on E; 4A^3+27B^2 = -62500 and 36 does not divide 62500; the [2] exclusion mod 5 is correct (2 is a non-residue mod 5).
consistency_checks_passed: Non-effectivity: a single-fold representation implies Matiyasevich's 1974 non-effectivizable estimates; the paper's constants (P, c_E, kappa, m_*, u_0, l) are effectively computable in principle, so non-effectivity comes from the r.e. set, not from the construction. No conflict.
Davis's quartic equation route and the Shanks-Wagstaff conjecture are unaffected (different route).
